char-kukri-mukri.desc: Char Kukri Mukri lies off Char Fasson where the Meghna and Tentulia meet the Bay of Bengal. Much of it is planted mangrove forest, flooded by every high tide, and it is protected as a wildlife sanctuary. Deer, monkeys, otters and many birds live here, and the forest's channels can be explored by boat. Nearby chars have long, quiet beaches.
blocks: How to get there
Launch from Dhaka to Bhola or Char Fasson, road to Char Kachhpia, then trawler to the island.
Good to know
Facilities are limited; book the rest house or go with an organised group. Check tide times and avoid trips in rough weather or cyclone season.

bhola-buffalo-bathan.desc: On Bhola's chars, herders keep buffalo in open grazing camps called bathan. The animals swim between islands, graze on grass at low tide and are milked by herders who live in simple huts. The milk travels by boat to town to become the famous curd. It is a way of life tied closely to the rhythm of the river.
blocks: Good to know
Herders are usually happy to talk; ask before photographing and don't approach the animals closely.

jacob-tower.desc: Built in the 2010s in Char Fasson town, Jacob Tower is a tall observation tower named after a local politician. From the top you look across flat green fields, the town and the river channels to the south. On clear winter days the view reaches far over the island. It is an easy stop before heading to the chars.
blocks: How to get there
In Char Fasson town, reached by bus from Bhola town (about 2 hrs).
Good to know
Go on a clear day; avoid when windy.

tarua-beach.desc: Tarua beach lies on Dhal Char at the southern end of Bhola, facing the Bay of Bengal. Long sands, red crabs and forest behind the shore make it a favourite of campers. Winter brings migratory shorebirds. Getting here takes effort, so you will likely share it only with fishermen.
blocks: How to get there
From Char Fasson, travel to Char Kachhpia and take a trawler to Dhal Char; often combined with Char Kukri Mukri.
Good to know
Go with a local guide or organised camping group; carry water and food; avoid rough weather and cyclone signals.

mostafa-kamal-memorial-museum.desc: Sepoy Mohammad Mostafa Kamal was born in this part of Bhola, and the village is now called Mostafa Nagar after him. In 2008 the government built a memorial library and museum here as part of a project at the birthplaces of the seven Bir Sreshthos and the language martyrs. A few personal items and photographs are shown beside shelves of books on the Liberation War and other subjects. Recent reports describe the place as poorly kept, with few visitors and a thin collection. It is still a meaningful stop for anyone interested in 1971.
blocks: How to get there
It is in Mostafa Nagar, Alinagar union, about 7 km from Bhola town; take an auto or CNG.
Good to know
It is listed as open 10 am–4 pm except public holidays, but staffing is thin, so ask locally before going. Pair it with the Independence Museum on the same day.

monpura-island.desc: Monpura is a separate island upazila east of the Bhola mainland, set in the wide Meghna. Its villages, fishing ghats and stretches of mangrove plantation give it a slow, isolated rhythm. Herds of buffalo graze on surrounding chars, and spotted deer can sometimes be seen in the forest. Sunrise and sunset over the open water are the main events.
blocks: How to get there
Direct launches from Dhaka Sadarghat, or boats from Tazumuddin in Bhola.
Good to know
River crossings get rough in the monsoon; travel in winter and carry cash, as banking is limited.

glance: Bazars in Bhola town, Char Fasson and Lalmohan
bhola-mohisher-doi.desc: Buffalo herds grazing on Bhola's chars produce rich milk that is set into curd in clay pots. Unlike sweet mishti doi, mohisher doi is mostly sour, with a thick, creamy layer on top. Locals eat it with chira and gur, or simply with sugar after a meal. It is served at weddings and sold at bazars across the island.

glance: River ghats and local hotels across Bhola
bhola-meghna-ilish.desc: Bhola's fishing fleets work the Meghna and Tentulia, among the richest hilsa waters in the country. At landing ghats like those near Tazumuddin and Char Fasson, the catch comes ashore every morning in season. Small hotels fry it fresh or cook it in mustard gravy. Note the government's breeding-season fishing bans, when hilsa should not be caught or sold.

bhola-independence-museum.desc: The museum stands in the Fatema Khanom Complex at Banglabazar, about 10 km south of Bhola town, and was opened in January 2018. Its three floors move through history in order: the anti-British movement, Partition and the Language Movement on the first, the road to 1971 on the second, and the Liberation War with recordings of Bangabandhu's speeches on the third. Rare photographs and documents sit alongside touch screens and a multimedia hall. There is also a library and research corner. The surrounding complex includes a mosque, college and other institutions on landscaped grounds.
blocks: How to get there
From Bhola town take an auto or CNG south along the Char Fasson road to Banglabazar (about 10 km).
Good to know
Allow time for the top floor, where the audio and video material is. A good rainy-day stop before heading south to the chars.
